epic.title: Local Developer Experience
epic.description: Everything in spec §18 built on top of the LocalStack dev environment: the 60-second `make demo`, a three-region local simulation with simulated CRR/Global Tables replication plus partition and failover exercises, FakeClock-based time travel, deterministic named fixtures, dual REPLs (evcxr and mtcctl), hot reload, and the self-documenting make target suite. Per §25.7 dev-experience tickets are first-class: this epic is the velocity substrate for every other epic, for both humans and agents, and everything runs on a laptop at zero cloud cost (§1).

tickets.title: Makefile target-suite skeleton with self-documenting help and stub targets
tickets.description:
## Goal
Establish the top-level Makefile target suite (§18.8) as the single entry point for all dev workflows: every target from the spec table is declared up front, delegating to `scripts/` or cargo, so later tickets across all epics wire in implementations without restructuring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Top-level `Makefile` declares every target in the §18.8 table (`demo`, `demo-multiregion`, `test*`, `repl`, `fixture-load/save`, `time-advance`, `partition-region`, `api-gen`, `codemap`, `agent-context`, `agent-precheck`, `verify-task`, `journal`, `lint`, `fmt`, `audit`, `bench`, `doctor`) plus lifecycle companions `dev`, `demo-down`, `demo-multiregion-down`
- Implemented targets delegate to `scripts/<name>.sh` or cargo; unimplemented targets print "not implemented yet — tracked in beads" and exit non-zero
- `make help` (default target) self-documents all targets from `##` comments
- Parameterized targets accept args per spec (`name=X`, `days=N`, `msg="..."`)
- Conventions documented in `docs/dev-environment.md` so other epics add targets consistently

## Out of Scope
- Implementations behind any target (owned by follow-on tickets across epics)
- CI job definitions (§22.13, foundation-infra)

## Testing
- E2E: shell smoke test in `tests/e2e/make-targets.sh` asserts `make help` lists all §18.8 targets and stubs exit non-zero

## Demo
`make help` shows the full annotated target catalog; `make demo` prints a friendly not-implemented pointer to its beads ticket.

tickets.title: make doctor: dev environment diagnostics with actionable remediation
tickets.description:
## Goal
Implement `make doctor` (§18.8): diagnose the dev environment and print actionable remediation so onboarding failures are self-explaining instead of mysterious.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `scripts/doctor.sh` (wired to `make doctor`) checks: Docker daemon reachable, Compose v2 present, required ports free (LocalStack 4566, admin UI 8080), rustc/cargo match `rust-toolchain.toml`, `cargo-watch` and `evcxr_repl` installed, SoftHSM2 library present, LocalStack image pulled, sufficient free disk
- Each check prints PASS/FAIL/WARN with a one-line copy-pasteable remediation command
- Exit code 0 only when all hard checks pass; WARN-only exits 0
- Runs in <10 s; no network calls beyond the local Docker socket
- Check list is data-driven so later tickets append checks in one place

## Out of Scope
- Auto-fixing the environment (doctor only diagnoses)
- CI environment validation (ci-pipeline owns its own images)

## Testing
- Unit: check functions exercised with stubbed commands (bats/shell harness)
- E2E: `make doctor` runs green in the CI container

## Demo
On a fresh machine run `make doctor` — see failing checks with copy-pasteable fixes; after applying them, all green.

tickets.title: Clock trait, SystemClock, and thread-safe FakeClock crate
tickets.description:
## Goal
Provide the injected `Clock` trait, `SystemClock`, and a thread-safe `FakeClock` with controllable advancement (§22.11) — the foundation for time travel (§18.4) and deterministic time-dependent tests across all epics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New crate `crates/clock`: `pub trait Clock: Send + Sync { fn now(&self) -> SystemTime; }` plus `SystemClock` and `FakeClock`
- `FakeClock::advance(Duration)` and `set(SystemTime)`; monotonicity enforced (never goes backward); `Arc<FakeClock>` shareable across threads
- Optional tokio feature: fake-clock-driven sleep/interval helpers for cadence-based loops
- Clippy `disallowed-methods` denies `SystemTime::now()`/`Instant::now()` outside `crates/clock` and test code (§22.12, rule `no-systemtime-now-in-prod` §23.2)
- Docs show the injection pattern (`Arc<dyn Clock>`, §22.7) with a worked example

## Out of Scope
- Migrating other crates' call sites (adopting epics own that)
- Admin API control endpoints (`dev-time-advance`)

## Testing
- Unit: advancement, monotonicity, cross-thread visibility
- Loom: concurrent advance/now interleavings on FakeClock internals
- Property: a sequence of advances yields the same final `now()` regardless of interleaving order

## Demo
`cargo test -p clock`; doc example shows a batch-cadence loop firing instantly under FakeClock instead of waiting wall-clock time.

tickets.title: make repl: evcxr Rust REPL with workspace crates pre-loaded
tickets.description:
## Goal
Ship `make repl` (§18.6, §18.8): an `evcxr` Rust REPL with workspace crates pre-loaded for ad-hoc human exploration (OQ-10 resolution: evcxr provided; CLI REPL is primary for agents).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make repl` verifies/installs `evcxr_repl` and launches it with an init file (`scripts/repl-init.evcxr`)
- Init pre-loads core workspace crates via `:dep` path dependencies and a prelude importing common types (tree, serialization, clock)
- Startup banner shows how to build a toy tree and compute an inclusion proof in ~3 lines
- `scripts/check-repl-init.sh` fails if the init references a crate missing from the workspace (kept honest as crates are added)
- Documented in `docs/dev-environment.md` with known evcxr limitations

## Out of Scope
- `mtcctl repl` CLI shell (`dev-repl-cli`)
- Jupyter kernel setup

## Testing
- Unit: none (glue)
- E2E: nightly-lane CI job evaluates the init file headlessly and runs one tree-building snippet

## Demo
`make repl` → paste the banner snippet → see a Merkle root computed interactively.

tickets.title: Seeded deterministic synthetic entry generator
tickets.description:
## Goal
A seeded, deterministic synthetic entry generator producing valid MTC assertion/entry inputs for fixtures (§18.5), the demo issuance loop (§18.1), and soak/perf tests — same seed, byte-identical stream, every run, every platform.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/dev-entrygen`: `EntryGen::new(seed)` yields an infinite iterator of valid entries (domains, keys, claims) using a seeded RNG (e.g. `rand_chacha`)
- Determinism: same seed produces identical serialized bytes across runs and platforms
- Generated entries pass domain-type validation and serialization round-trip (§19.2)
- Supports shaped generation: fixed count, DNS name patterns, key-type mix
- CLI shim (`cargo run -p dev-entrygen -- --seed 42 --count 1000`) emitting JSONL

## Out of Scope
- Driving the CA pipeline (fixture generator tickets own that)
- Malformed/adversarial inputs (fuzzing, §19.3, testing epic)

## Testing
- Unit: shape parameters honored; count semantics
- Property: determinism across seeds; every generated entry satisfies `parse(serialize(x)) == x`

## Demo
Run the CLI shim twice with `--seed 42 --count 3` → byte-identical output; pipe entries into the intake path once it exists.

tickets.title: Fixture snapshot/restore engine for LocalStack S3 and DynamoDB state
tickets.description:
## Goal
Core fixture snapshot/restore engine (§18.5): capture LocalStack S3 and DynamoDB state as a named, versioned artifact and restore it byte-identically — the substrate for every named fixture and bug-repro workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `crates/dev-fixture` library + CLI: `fixture save <name>` dumps all S3 buckets (object versions and Object Lock metadata included) and all DDB tables into `fixtures/<name>/` with a manifest (schema version, per-file checksums, created-at, generator provenance)
- `fixture load <name>` wipes target LocalStack state and restores; idempotent; verifies manifest checksums before applying and aborts on mismatch
- Round-trip: save → load → save produces identical checksums
- Clear error naming the schema version on unsupported manifests
- Payloads stored as compressed tarballs; storage policy (git-lfs vs regenerate-on-demand) documented in `docs/dev-environment.md`

## Out of Scope
- SoftHSM token capture and `make` wiring (`dev-fixture-targets`)
- Named fixture content (million-entries etc. — separate tickets per §25.6)

## Testing
- Unit: manifest serialization, checksum verification
- Integration: round-trip against LocalStack; S3 versioning + Object Lock metadata survive restore (§19.1)

## Demo
Write objects/rows to the local stack, `fixture save scratch`, wipe, `fixture load scratch` → endpoint listings show identical state.

tickets.title: SoftHSM token capture and make fixture-save/fixture-load wiring
tickets.description:
## Goal
Complete the fixture workflow (§18.5, §18.8): capture the SoftHSM token directory alongside storage state and wire `make fixture-save name=X` / `make fixture-load name=X`, so a restored fixture is a fully working CA (signing keys included).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixture engine extended to include the SoftHSM token directory in the payload and manifest; restore reinstates it so checkpoint signing works immediately after load
- `make fixture-save name=X` / `make fixture-load name=X` wired per Makefile conventions; missing `name=` fails with usage help
- Loading while services run follows a documented safe sequence (quiesce/restart hint printed) rather than silently corrupting state
- Round-trip: demo state saved, wiped, loaded → `mtcctl status` reports the identical tree head and signing works

## Out of Scope
- Engine internals for S3/DDB (`dev-fixture-engine`)
- Multi-region fixture topologies

## Testing
- Integration: SoftHSM token round-trip; post-restore signing succeeds (§19.1)
- E2E: `tests/e2e/fixture-roundtrip.sh` save/wipe/load smoke via the make targets (§19.13)

## Demo
Issue a few certs in the demo env, `make fixture-save name=scratch`, wipe, `make fixture-load name=scratch` → identical state via `mtcctl status`.

tickets.title: make demo: 60-second single-region demo orchestration with dev-mode profile
tickets.description:
## Goal
Ship the 60-second demo (§18.1): `make demo` brings up LocalStack, SoftHSM2, the CA service in dev mode, and the admin UI from a fresh clone with one command — the flagship promise of §1 and the Phase 3 roadmap exit criterion (§24).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo` orchestrates: compose bring-up (via localstack-dev-env), SoftHSM token init + key generation, resource provisioning (buckets/tables), CA service launch with dev-mode profile, admin UI reachable at `localhost:8080`
- Dev-mode profile (`config/dev.toml`): fast batch cadence (seconds), SoftHSM PKCS#11, looser timing — consumed by the CA service's config loading
- Readiness gating: returns only when health endpoints (§20.5) report ready, with per-component progress output
- `make demo-down` tears down cleanly; re-running `make demo` is idempotent
- Warm start (images pulled, workspace built) completes in <60 s on a dev laptop
- Any component failure names the component and points at `make doctor`

## Out of Scope
- Auto-issuing ACME loop (`dev-demo-issuance-loop`); self-auditor wiring (`dev-audit-demo-wiring`)
- FakeClock wiring (`dev-time-advance`); multi-region topology (`dev-multiregion-harness`)

## Testing
- Integration: provisioning scripts against LocalStack
- E2E: bring-up/tear-down smoke (formal CI gate lands in `dev-demo-smoke`)

## Demo
`git clone && make demo` → open `localhost:8080`, watch batches advance; `mtcctl status` shows a live CA.
deps: EXTERNAL:runnable CA service dev-mode binary (ca-service epic)
EXTERNAL:admin UI shell served at localhost:8080 (admin-surface epic)

tickets.title: Sample ACME client auto-issuing certs in a loop for make demo
tickets.description:
## Goal
Complete the §18.1 demo loop: a sample ACME client that auto-issues certificates continuously so `make demo` shows a living CA (batches filling, tree growing) with zero manual input.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Demo issuer (sidecar process/container started by `make demo`) drives the ACME endpoint in a loop using seeded names from `dev-entrygen`
- Rate configurable via the dev profile (default ~1 cert per 2 s); clean shutdown with `make demo-down`
- Issued certs visible in the admin UI and via `mtcctl cert list` within one dev-mode batch interval
- `DEMO_ISSUER=off make demo` disables the loop for quiet debugging
- Loop logs are structured and prefixed so demo output stays readable

## Out of Scope
- ACME endpoint implementation (ca-service epic)
- Load/soak-level issuance rates (§19.7, testing epic)

## Testing
- Unit: rate limiter / backoff logic
- Integration: one loop iteration issues successfully against the dev stack
- E2E: demo smoke asserts cert count increases over a 30 s window

## Demo
`make demo` → admin UI batch view fills with new entries every few seconds without touching anything.

tickets.title: CI demo smoke test enforcing the 60-second budget
tickets.description:
## Goal
CI-enforced smoke test and timing budget for the demo (§18.1): prove `make demo` works from a clean checkout and stays fast, so the flagship 60-second promise never rots.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `tests/e2e/demo-smoke.sh`: runs `make demo`, waits for readiness, asserts admin UI returns 200, `mtcctl status` succeeds, at least one signed checkpoint exists, then `make demo-down` leaves no containers
- Records wall-clock bring-up time; fails if warm start exceeds 60 s (budget constant defined in one place; cold image pulls excluded from the hard gate)
- Wired as a required CI job (§22.13) using cached images and a prebuilt workspace
- On failure, per-component logs dumped as CI artifacts
- Script passes shellcheck

## Out of Scope
- Multi-region smoke (`dev-multiregion-harness` ships its own)
- Full issuance-path E2E scenario suites (§19.13, testing epic)

## Testing
- E2E: this ticket is the E2E layer for the demo path

## Demo
CI run shows "demo-smoke: PASS (42 s)"; locally `tests/e2e/demo-smoke.sh` gives the same verdict.

tickets.title: make dev: cargo-watch hot reload of the CA service
tickets.description:
## Goal
`make dev` hot reload (§18.7): `cargo-watch` rebuilds and restarts the CA service on source change while LocalStack/SoftHSM stay up, keeping the edit→observe loop at seconds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make dev` starts (or reuses) the demo infrastructure, then runs the CA service in the foreground under `cargo watch` with debounce
- Watches `crates/`; ignores `target/`, `fixtures/`, `docs/`
- Restarted service re-attaches to existing LocalStack state — no re-provisioning; admin UI reflects the restart within one refresh
- Rebuild-to-serving latency for a one-line change measured by the E2E script and documented in `docs/dev-environment.md` (target: a few seconds in debug mode per §18.7)
- Works alongside the demo issuance loop (issuer retries through restarts)

## Out of Scope
- Admin UI asset live-reload (admin-surface epic)
- Watch-triggered test runs (developers use `cargo watch -x test` ad hoc)

## Testing
- Unit: none (glue)
- E2E: script touches a source file, asserts the service process is replaced and health returns ready

## Demo
`make dev`, edit a log line in the batch builder, save → service restarts in seconds and the new line appears in output.

tickets.title: Time travel: dev-mode clock admin API and make time-advance
tickets.description:
## Goal
Time travel (§18.4): dev-mode admin API control of the FakeClock plus `make time-advance days=N`, enabling instant exploration of expiry, batch cadence, and retention behavior without waiting wall-clock time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dev-only admin API routes (enabled only in dev mode): `POST /dev/clock/advance` accepting `{days|hours|seconds}`, `GET /dev/clock` returning simulated now; absent/404 in non-dev builds
- Dev-mode wiring hands the shared `FakeClock` instance to the CA service's `Arc<dyn Clock>` injection point so cadence loops and validity checks respond immediately to advancement
- `make time-advance days=N` calls the endpoint and prints old → new simulated time
- Advancing past certificate validity windows makes them expire, observable via `mtcctl` and the admin UI
- OpenAPI spec updated for the dev routes (§17.2 codegen pipeline)

## Out of Scope
- FakeClock primitive (`dev-fake-clock`)
- Time-triggered pruning/retention flows (pruning epic verifies using this tool)

## Testing
- Unit: route handlers, dev-mode gating
- Integration: advancing during a running dev stack shifts the next batch timestamp
- E2E: `make time-advance days=400` → previously valid cert reported expired (§18.4)

## Demo
`make demo`, issue a cert, `make time-advance days=400`, `mtcctl cert lookup` shows it expired — under a minute of wall time.
deps: EXTERNAL:CA service reads time via injected Arc<dyn Clock> (ca-service epic)

tickets.title: mtcctl repl: interactive, scriptable CLI command shell
tickets.description:
## Goal
`mtcctl repl` (§18.6): an interactive, scriptable command shell over the full mtcctl command tree — the agent-preferred REPL (OQ-10): deterministic, output-captured, no per-command process spawn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `mtcctl repl` starts a readline loop (history, Ctrl-D exit) dispatching lines through the existing clap command tree in-process, reusing one API client connection
- Non-interactive: `mtcctl repl --script file` and piped stdin execute line-by-line, echoing commands; stop-on-error by default with `--keep-going` override
- Deterministic output: no ANSI when stdout is not a TTY; `--output json` respected per command; each command's output delimited for machine parsing
- Built-ins: `help`, `exit`; a failing command does not kill the interactive session
- Exit code reflects last (or first failing) command in script mode

## Out of Scope
- New admin operations (only re-exposes existing commands)
- evcxr REPL (`dev-repl-evcxr`)

## Testing
- Unit: line parsing, dispatch, stop-on-error semantics
- E2E: shell test pipes a script through `mtcctl repl` against the demo stack and asserts delimited JSON outputs (§19.13)

## Demo
`mtcctl repl` → `status`, `batch list`, `cert issue --domain demo.test` interactively; then the same via `--script` with byte-identical output.
deps: EXTERNAL:mtcctl CLI scaffolding with clap command tree (admin-surface epic)

tickets.title: million-entries fixture: deterministic large-log snapshot
tickets.description:
## Goal
The `million-entries` fixture (§18.5): a deterministic large-log snapshot for performance testing, realistic demos, and reproducing bugs that only appear at depth.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generator (xtask or script) drives the batch builder + tree updater directly (bypassing ACME) with seeded entries from `dev-entrygen`, under FakeClock acceleration
- Produces exactly 1,000,000 entries; final tree head is byte-stable across regenerations (expected root documented)
- Saved via the fixture framework as `fixtures/million-entries` with provenance (seed, generator version) in the manifest
- `make fixture-load name=million-entries` restores it and a sampled inclusion proof verifies via `mtcctl log inclusion`
- Generation is streamed (bounded memory) and completes in documented, laptop-feasible time

## Out of Scope
- Fixture engine changes (`dev-fixture-engine`, `dev-fixture-targets`)
- Benchmarks consuming the fixture (`make bench`, testing epic)

## Testing
- Integration: reduced-size (10k) generation asserted byte-stable in CI; full 1M run in the nightly lane
- E2E: load fixture → sampled inclusion proofs verify via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=million-entries` → admin UI shows a 1M-entry tree; proof verification round-trips instantly.

tickets.title: Dev-experience documentation: quickstart, target catalog, troubleshooting
tickets.description:
## Goal
Documentation for the dev experience (§18): fresh-clone quickstart, the full make-target catalog, and troubleshooting — making the "everything runnable on a laptop" goal (§1) discoverable without tribal knowledge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README quickstart: clone → `make doctor` → `make demo` → open `localhost:8080`, with expected-output snippets
- `docs/dev-environment.md` documents every §18.8 target with purpose, args, and owning component; kept in sync via the `make help` smoke test
- Troubleshooting section maps common failures to `make doctor` checks and fixes
- Walkthroughs for each dev-experience feature shipped at time of writing (time travel §18.4, fixtures §18.5, REPLs §18.6, hot reload §18.7), extended as later targets land
- Verified by a scripted fresh-clone run in a clean container

## Out of Scope
- Agent-facing context docs (`AGENTS.md`, §23 — agent-harnessing epic)
- Operational runbooks (§21.2, observability epic)

## Testing
- E2E: quickstart commands executed verbatim by a CI script (doc-drift guard)
- Lint: markdown link check

## Demo
Hand the README to someone new: they reach a running CA and issue a cert without asking a single question.

tickets.title: Local CRR and Global Tables replication simulator with configurable lag
tickets.description:
## Goal
Local replication simulator (§18.3): simulated S3 CRR and DynamoDB Global Tables replication between LocalStack instances with configurable lag — the substrate the three-region environment is built on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replicator binary (`crates/dev-replicator`) copies new S3 object versions source→target (polling ListObjectVersions), preserving keys, version order, and Object Lock metadata
- DDB replication tails the source table (Streams or scan-diff) and applies to target with last-writer-wins parity to Global Tables semantics
- Configurable per-link lag (`REPL_LAG_MS`); pause/resume via signal or local control endpoint (the partition hook)
- Emits a replication-lag log line/metric per link
- Runs as N instances for arbitrary directed-link topologies

## Out of Scope
- Three-region compose topology (`dev-multiregion-harness`)
- Production CRR/Global Tables configuration in CDK (foundation-infra)

## Testing
- Unit: dedup/ordering, lag scheduling
- Integration: two LocalStack containers — object written to A appears in B after the lag, not before; pause halts propagation
- Property: applying the same event stream twice is idempotent

## Demo
Start two LocalStacks + replicator with 5 s lag; `aws s3 cp` to A; watch the object appear in B five seconds later.

tickets.title: make demo-multiregion: three-region local simulation environment
tickets.description:
## Goal
`make demo-multiregion` (§18.3): three local region stacks (us-east-1 primary; us-west-2, eu-west-1 standby) with simulated CRR and Global Tables replication — the roadmap's "multi-region simulation in dev environment" (§24 Phase 5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Compose topology: per-region LocalStack + CA service instance with region-scoped config and ports (admin UIs on 8080/8081/8082), plus replicator instances matching the production CRR fan-out
- Primary holds the lease and issues; standbys run read-only mode and serve status (lease/epoch protocol)
- `make demo-multiregion` gates on all three regions healthy; `make demo-multiregion-down` cleans up fully; idempotent re-runs
- Smoke: a cert issued in the primary is visible from a standby's state within the configured lag bound
- Region set and lag configurable in one file; defaults documented

## Out of Scope
- Partition and failover scenarios (`dev-partition-failover-scenarios`)
- Chaos test suite (§19.9, testing epic)

## Testing
- Integration: replicator wiring per link
- E2E: bring-up smoke asserting the lease is held by exactly one region and standby replication lag is within bound

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion` → three admin UIs side by side; issue in us-east-1, watch the entry surface in eu-west-1 seconds later.

tickets.title: make partition-region and scripted local failover exercise
tickets.description:
## Goal
Partition simulation and the scripted failover exercise (§18.3, §13): `make partition-region X` / `make heal-region X` plus an end-to-end local failover demo driven by `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make partition-region X` disconnects region X's containers from the shared network and pauses its replicator links; `make heal-region X` restores both
- Partitioned primary loses lease renewal; standbys keep serving reads (observable in admin UIs)
- `tests/e2e/failover-demo.sh`: partition us-east-1 → `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2` → issuance resumes in the new primary at a bumped epoch; on heal, writes from the old primary are rejected (no split-brain, lease/epoch invariants §13)
- Scenario is re-runnable without full environment teardown
- Both targets no-op with a clear message when the multi-region environment is not running

## Out of Scope
- Failover command implementation (multi-region + admin-surface epics)
- Automated failover (explicit non-goal, §1)

## Testing
- Integration: network disconnect/heal mechanics
- E2E: the failover demo script in the nightly lane (§19.13)

## Demo
`make demo-multiregion`, `make partition-region us-east-1`, `mtcctl failover initiate --to us-west-2` → watch us-west-2 take over issuance live.

tickets.title: Wire self-auditor into make demo and add make audit
tickets.description:
## Goal
Wire the self-auditor into the local demo (§18.1) and add `make audit` (§18.8), so every demo run continuously demonstrates the transparency story (§25.8) on a laptop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `make demo` starts the self-auditor on a periodic dev-mode interval (from the dev profile) against the local stack
- `make audit` triggers one full audit pass on demand and prints a human-readable verdict summary
- Audit results surface in the admin UI audit view and via `mtcctl`
- A dev-only corruption helper script damages one tile; the next audit pass fails loudly, naming the tile — the documented "seeing is believing" check
- Auditor log lines are clearly attributed in demo output

## Out of Scope
- Self-auditor implementation (observability epic)
- Compliance report generation (§20.3)

## Testing
- Integration: auditor pass against demo-stack state
- E2E: demo smoke extended — audit verdict OK; corruption helper flips it to FAIL

## Demo
`make demo` → `make audit` prints PASS; run the corruption helper, `make audit` prints FAIL identifying the corrupted tile.
deps: EXTERNAL:self-auditor runnable locally in dev mode (observability epic)

tickets.title: with-revocations fixture: deterministic revoked-cert snapshot
tickets.description:
## Goal
The `with-revocations` fixture (§18.5): a deterministic snapshot containing issued-then-revoked certificates, for reproducing revocation-path bugs and demoing revocation checking.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generator seeds a modest log (~10k entries) via `dev-entrygen`, then revokes a deterministic subset (~1%) through the local revocation flow
- Saved via the fixture framework as `fixtures/with-revocations` with seed and revoked-set provenance in the manifest
- Regeneration is byte-stable; expected tree head and revocation-set hash documented
- `make fixture-load name=with-revocations` → `mtcctl` reports revoked certs as revoked and the rest as valid
- Generation completes in CI-feasible time (<5 min)

## Out of Scope
- Revocation mechanics (revocation epic, §16)
- Post-pruning fixture (`dev-fixture-post-pruning`)

## Testing
- Integration: regeneration byte-stability check
- E2E: load fixture → revocation status assertions via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=with-revocations` → `mtcctl cert lookup` on a known-revoked serial reports revoked instantly.

tickets.title: post-pruning fixture: deterministic pruned-log snapshot
tickets.description:
## Goal
The `post-pruning` fixture (§18.5): a deterministic snapshot of a log after pruning has run, for validating that proofs for retained entries survive pruning and making pruning-adjacent bugs reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Generator builds a seeded log, advances the FakeClock past retention windows (using the `dev-time-advance` machinery), and runs the local pruning workflow to completion
- Saved via the fixture framework as `fixtures/post-pruning` with provenance (seed, pruned range, retention config) in the manifest
- Regeneration byte-stable; expected head and pruned-range boundaries documented
- Loaded state verifies: inclusion proof for a retained entry passes while the pruned range is absent from storage yet the tree head remains valid (§19.2 pruning invariant)
- `make fixture-load name=post-pruning` completes in seconds

## Out of Scope
- Pruning workflow implementation (pruning epic, §15)
- Object Lock retention enforcement E2E (§15.3, pruning epic)

## Testing
- Integration: regeneration byte-stability
- E2E: load → sampled proof for a retained entry verifies via CLI (§19.13)

## Demo
`make fixture-load name=post-pruning` → admin UI shows pruned ranges; `mtcctl log inclusion` on a retained entry verifies.
